details.observed: The source and hierarchy cells now prove that the authored binding itself exists and is structurally intact. Dispatch physical W/A and Space; observe no authoritative living-state transition while the fixture continues visually.

Stop in a stable inspectable state and bind idle, nonzero-velocity movement, dash onset/recovery, authorized cast and accepted hurt to the authored AnimationPlayer and framebuffer.
Then separately retain the already-supported death/victory terminal holds and Retry reset receipts.

preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `native_godot_project` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

Keep frozen technical baseline `host_godot_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Make the release candidate closure-ready by restoring audible bounded footsteps, hardening representative final-wave performance and retry lifecycle, and completing a natural seven-to-ten-minute release route that exposes living Warden animation states without disturbing accepted presentation or authoritative systems.

diagnosis.root_cause: Release convergence is blocked by one confirmed product defect and two qualification-path failures. Footstep authorizations increment but the retained long walking source produces no Effects source event or audible output. The Warden's seven semantic mappings and deformation owner are structurally intact; repeated work failed because testing remained in a terminal-held victory fixture instead of a fresh living run. Dense-run timing was contaminated by llvmpipe and screenshot driving, while the complete-run check lacks an uninterrupted natural victory route, three natural builds, credits, and replay evidence. The next strategy must stop adding generic telemetry or retuning accepted animation transforms and instead repair actual mixed output, isolate living animation states through the ordinary route, and qualify real dense and complete play.

stop_conditions: Stop and repair before proceeding if native project validation or host boot develops any fatal Godot, GDScript, resource-load, or recurring runtime error.

Do not replace or restructure the accepted cemetery package, Warden package, semantic animation profile, camera compositor, HUD shell, or three weapon identities without new candidate-bound evidence of package-level incompatibility.
Do not claim footstep completion from semantic counters, source duration, or configured playback windows alone; actual Effects and Master output plus source-event causality are required.
Do not claim performance completion from llvmpipe, screenshot-driven, editor-stalled, paused, or empty-arena timing samples.

Do not claim complete-run or animation completion from diagnostic wave jumps, prepared result fixtures, terminal-held boss state, or setup actions; ordinary gameplay must cause the route and state transitions.

End the iteration when all three required release-convergence checks pass while native_godot_project and host_godot_boot remain passing, or stop with the exact unresolved candidate-side predicate and preserve all accepted baselines.

strategy.rationale: Use three independent closure passes: repair the footstep signal at the actual audio-output boundary; profile and optimize real dense gameplay without capture interference; and qualify the complete natural route from a fresh living state. For the repeated animation item, explicitly isolate the valid ordinary-run state instead of altering the already-proven semantic profile or repeating transform tuning.

code: GameLoop Runtime reruns validate:native_godot_project and validate:host_godot_boot; both must remain pass.

Developer performs focused static inspection of modified audio, dense-run, lifecycle, route, animation-wrapper, resource, and provenance files; no release export may bind editor-only validation actions.
Runtime logs contain no fatal or recurring GDScript errors, invalid freed-instance access, duplicate terminal commits, stale targets, NaN movement, stuck pause ownership, or resource-load failures.
runtime: Tester captures an isolated fresh-run footstep sequence on Effects and Master: movement tap, sustained movement, direction change, release, and idle tail, paired with source-event and owner-occupancy state.

Tester profiles the advancing representative final wave at 1920×1080 on the designated representative renderer without screenshot activity during the sample, then repeats the same workload through three prepare/advance/reset or complete Retry cycles.

Tester completes an uninterrupted ordinary title-to-victory run in 420–600 seconds, a natural failure-to-Retry branch, and three ordinary build paths; diagnostic preparation cannot satisfy these cells.

Tester captures fresh-run Warden state receipts for idle, move, dash onset/recovery, cast, hurt, death, victory, and Retry reset, pairing authoritative state, active authored clip, terminal ownership, and normal-input causality before deciding the animation issue or criterion verdicts.
visual: At 1920×1080, compare shipped-camera baseline and dense final-wave frames for player safe-frame visibility, escape lane, four enemy roles, Bellkeeper, pickups, friendly attacks, hostile telegraphs, boss health, and compact HUD readability.

Capture the ordinary route's title, living gameplay, upgrade draft, dense final wave, Bellkeeper phase transition, victory result, failure result, and Credits & Notices states; reject placeholders, debug presentation, clipping, lost focus, or central-arena obstruction.

For Warden animation, capture representative gameplay frames at nonzero locomotion, dash onset/recovery, cast, hurt, death hold, victory hold, and post-Retry idle; preserve authored deformation, feet/ground contact, lantern attachment, silhouette, and camera composition.

done_when: A physical movement tap in a fresh living run creates at least one recognizable, non-silent footstep source transition on Effects and audible output on both Effects and Master; music alone cannot satisfy the measurement.
Sustained movement and direction changes produce discrete bounded footsteps without looping speech, hum, or an exposed multi-second tail; each event retires at its declared short window.
The movement owner never exceeds two simultaneous voices, and release, pause, result, Retry, and Title leave no stale footstep player or movement-owned voice.
Critical warnings, player hurt, upgrade selection, weapon feedback, music transitions, and existing audio bus ownership remain intact.
Any newly bound source is an intact redistributable recording with candidate-owned provenance and notices; no generated tone substitutes for a recorded footstep.
tasks.instructions: Repair the footstep path at the actual stream/output boundary. Retain the existing allocation-before-free-voice behavior, movement-owner cap, semantic cadence, bus separation, and lifecycle retirement. Audition the configured offsets against the retained recording; if its usable regions still produce silence, bind an intact licensed short footstep recording selected by the Developer and update provenance. Verify the player receives the stream before play, the offset is legal, Effects routing is active, and the short playback window cannot suppress the source transition. Do not replace the broader licensed audio library, add a synthetic tone, or rebalance unrelated accepted semantic layers.
tasks.title: Restore audible bounded locomotion footsteps

done_when: At 1920×1080, the representative final-wave profile resolves 25–40 ordinary enemies, the Bellkeeper, all three weapon families, production pickups, animation, VFX, bounded lights, HUD, and audio during an advancing gameplay window.

A representative-hardware sample taken without screenshot-driving interference satisfies the stable-60-FPS contract and records renderer identity plus p50, p95, p99, worst frame time, sample count, and start/end workload counts.

Dense-work invariants remain bounded: one neighbor-grid rebuild per physics frame, no more than 12 neighbor candidates per query, no more than four admitted ordinary-enemy telegraphs, no more than eight ordinary role lights and three hurt lights, and no unbounded projectile, attack-ledger, pickup, effect, or audio-voice growth.

Three final-profile or complete-run Retry cycles return to an ordinary ready state with zero live enemies, boss, friendly attacks, pickups, impact effects, active effect voices, and stale neighbor registrations; persistent pool size and signal ownership do not grow between cycles.
The shipped gameplay view preserves the accepted warm-lantern/cool-moonlight hierarchy, player safe frame, dangerous telegraphs, weapon readability, and boss visibility under representative density.
tasks.instructions: Replace the prior contaminated qualification approach with a clean advancing profile using the existing prepared/advance/reset separation and passive ordinary-final-wave sampler. First identify a candidate-owned hotspot from a non-paused sample without screenshots or diagnostic mutation during the timing window; then optimize only the causally identified high-churn path. Prefer bounded scheduling, pooling, admission, and lifecycle repair over reducing required enemy density or degrading accepted presentation. Do not add another parallel profiler when current receipts already expose renderer, workload, work caps, and retry baselines. Preserve five-wave pacing and all accepted visual, animation, audio, HUD, and weapon identities.
tasks.title: Harden representative final-wave performance and lifecycle

done_when: An ordinary Play route, with no diagnostic jump or prepared terminal state, traverses all five authored wave IDs in order, introduces the required composition and elite changes, enters both Bellkeeper phases naturally, and reaches victory between 420 and 600 seconds.

The route supports at least three truthful viable build shapes assembled through ordinary three-card drafts; every accepted choice records concrete before/after values and visibly changes combat behavior.

Victory and failure each commit exactly one terminal snapshot containing time, level, defeated enemies, damage dealt, damage taken, equipped weapon ranks, and selected upgrades; Retry starts a clean living run and Title reaches the authored shell.
Credits & Notices is navigable through normal UI input and accurately points to complete candidate-owned provenance and third-party notices.

A fresh ordinary living run exposes idle, nonzero-velocity move, dash onset/recovery, authorized cast, and accepted hurt through the existing authored AnimationPlayer; death and victory hold only after their matching terminal transition, and Retry clears the terminal hold.

The structurally valid seven-state Warden semantic profile, deformation owner, model hierarchy, lantern attachment, camera compositor, cemetery presentation, HUD shell, and failure/result Retry flow remain unchanged unless fresh ordinary-run evidence identifies a narrow wrapper or state-ownership defect.
tasks.instructions: Exercise and finish the actual title-to-result product route rather than expanding diagnostic shortcuts. Tune only candidate behavior that prevents a natural seven-to-ten-minute run, truthful build progression, terminal statistics, credits, or clean replay. Treat the repeated Warden animation item as fixture/state isolation first: begin through Play or ordinary Retry, keep the run living and inspectable, and drive each living semantic through authoritative movement, dash, combat, and damage systems. Do not retune transforms, substitute clips, or rewrite the accepted semantic profile merely to create evidence; if a real defect appears, repair the narrow run-state-to-binding wrapper while preserving terminal death/victory holds.
